sports_foundation.title: P.E. Midterm Reviewer & Study Guide
sports_foundation.content: 1. Sports in Primitive Times & Ancient HistoryOrigins: Physical education historians believe primitive humans engaged in gymnastics-related activities such as tumbling, jumping, swimming, and group acrobatics early in history across various regions.Ancient China (c. 4000 BC): Artifacts suggest early participation in organized sporting activities.Ancient Egypt: Pharaoh monuments show that swimming, fishing, javelin throwing, high jump, and wrestling were well-developed and regulated thousands of years ago.Ancient Persia: Focused primarily on combative sports linked to military skills, such as the traditional Iranian martial art of Zurkhaneh.Ancient Greece & The Olympic Games:776 BC: The Greeks founded the first Olympic Games as a festival dedicated to Zeus.394 AD: The ancient games ended due to financial corruption.Gymnastics Addition: Gymnastics routines were integrated into the Olympics, encompassing boxing, throwing, jumping, track and field, and weightlifting (which later separated into individual sports).Resurgence: After ending in 394 AD, the games did not reappear in public arenas until the 16th century.2. Classifications of SportsA. According to Player Composition1. Individual Sports: Consists of a single player competing against an opponent.2. Dual Sports: Consists of a duo/pair competing against another duo/pair.3. Team Sports: Consists of three or more players per team.B. General CategorizationAthletics: Running, jumping, and throwing events.Ball Sports: Basketball, volleyball.Club-and-Ball Sports: Golf.Cue Sports: Billiards.Combat Sports: Taekwondo, Karatedo, Boxing, Wrestling.Dance Sport: Standard and Latin dance sports.Extreme Sports: BMX, Motocross.Gymnastics: Artistic and rhythmic gymnastics.Mind Sports: Chess.Racket Sports: Badminton, Table Tennis.Riding Sports: Equestrian.Shooting & Target Sports: Gun shooting.Water Sports: Swimming.Weight Sports: Weightlifting.Winter Sports: Figure/Ice Skating.Wheels Sports: Cycling.C. Examples of Individual and Dual SportsArchery, Arnis, Athletics, Bodybuilding, Badminton, Billiards, Boxing, Bowling, Diving, Chess, Cycling, Dance Sport, Darts, Equestrian, Fencing, Figure Skating, Golf, Gymnastics, Judo, Karatedo, Lawn Tennis, Motor Sports, Muay Thai, Shooting, Skateboarding, Skiing, Sepak Takraw, Snowboarding, Squash, Surfing, Swimming, Table Tennis, Taekwondo, Triathlon, Weightlifting, Wrestling.3. Key Sports TerminologiesAthletes: The players participating in sports.Athletics: Organized, highly structured, competitive activities involving skilled individuals.Coach: The formal authority figure within a team.Competition: A competitive sports event or tournament.Court: The physical facility or venue where games are played.Equipment: Heavy, well-built materials used in a sport.Exercise: Physical activity intended to participate, strengthen, or condition.Game: A match governed by rules and regulations; can also refer to non-sport recreational activities (e.g., card games, internet games).Leisure: Available time free from work, obligations, and responsibilities.Match: The entire game characterized by number, time, and order.Official: Individual or group holding full jurisdiction over the game.Play: Amusement engaged in for fun; non-utilitarian with unpredictable outcomes.Riot (Hooliganism): Violence in sports reflecting negative fan or player attitudes.Set: A specific partition of a match.Sportsmanship: An attitude prioritizing fair play, courtesy, ethical behavior, integrity, and grace in victory or defeat.Supplies: Consumable materials that require periodic replacement (e.g., racquets, balls).Team Captain: The designated player in charge of leading co-team members.Trainer: The instructor who teaches drills and skills.Uniform: Player clothing including shoes and mandatory accessories.4. Organization & Management of Sports in the PhilippinesA. Legal FoundationsRepublic Act No. 3138 (Sports Federation Law): Mandated that Philippine sports be governed by an autonomous national association with exclusive promotion control.Presidential Decree 604: Created the Ministry of Youth and Sports Development (MYSD). It authorized the Ministry of Education and Culture (now DepEd) to implement programs for youth, physical fitness, and sports.Executive Order No. 590: Issued by Pres. Ferdinand Marcos to transfer sports event management from barangay levels up to national meets under MYSD to elevate national sports quality (Palaro).B. Levels of Competition1. Amateur: Popular sports where participants represent a locality as ambassadors in structured games (e.g., National Games, SEA Games, Asian Games, Olympics).2. Professional: Profitable sports elevated to commercial entertainment (e.g., Manny Pacquiao in boxing, Michael Jordan in basketball).C. Hierarchy of Athletic Competitions1. Intramural Athletic Program: Competitions within the walls of a single school.2. Play Days: Community gatherings encouraging mass participation in stunts, games, and dances.3. Dual Meets: Competitions between two schools or two districts.4. Integrated Meets: Competitions combining public and private schools within a district.5. Regional Meet: Competitions between different school divisions within a region.6. Palarong Pambansa: The national championship between all 17 Philippine regions (including CAR and NCR).5. Athletic Meet Objectives & Personal RolesA. Objectives of an Athletic Meet1. Develop physical skills among potential athletes.2. Foster self-discipline, social maturity, emotional stability, and good sportsmanship.3. Educate the public regarding competitive sports.4. Promote health and constructive use of leisure time.5. Provide opportunities for social interaction among athletes.6. Build leadership and followership skills.B. Qualities of Leaders, Followers, & PlayersGood Leader: Shows sportsmanship, supports teammates, respects opponents, handles victory or defeat gracefully, knows all rules/limits, and stays patient with struggling teammates.Good Follower: Recognizes every member's value, follows leader suggestions, expresses opinions courteously, cooperates, and makes sacrifices for group success.Outstanding Player Traits:Psychological: High drive to succeed, motivation to improve skills/fitness, dedication to practice, alertness, competitive spirit, enthusiasm, self-control, industriousness, and good judgment.Physiological:Physical Size & Quickness: Essential baseline advantages.Strength: Developed via weight training or overload exercises.Power: Developed by using strength through a full range of motion with proper mechanics.Endurance: Developed through repeated exercise repetitions.Flexibility: Improved through static stretching; aids maneuvering, rebounding, and injury prevention.6. Game Officials & Their Roles1. Referee:Directs the game with final decision-making authority.Holds complete authority over all players and officials.Settles unwritten game scenarios and penalizes rule violations.2. Umpire:Decides center line crossing violations.Tracks official time-outs.Controls coach conduct and starting positions.Authorizes substitutions upon team captain request.Flags unsportsmanlike behavior and illegal body contact to the referee.3. Scorer:Stationed opposite the referee and behind the umpire.Records official scores, time-outs, and substitution logs.4. Linesmen:Monitors boundary lines (sidelines and end lines) on assigned field/court sides.
